primary_studies.title: Improved Object Detection Using a Robotic Sensing Antenna with Vibration Damping Control
primary_studies.where: §5.2, Fig. 10(a), Figs. 12–13; Table 5. Digital controller sample time in instrument description.
primary_studies.reference: A copper wire sits very near the steel cylinder. An encounter moves the wire to touch the cylinder; the resulting voltage transition is logged at a PCI-6229 digital input, independently of the load-cell signal used by the candidate detection algorithms. This is a physical closure benchmark. No per-event switch travel, hysteresis, bounce correction, independent calibration of first material contact, or uncertainty bound was verified. The controller has 1 ms sample time; this alone does not establish submillisecond alignment.
primary_studies.evidence: Table 5 reports means and standard deviations from 10 experiments at each orientation (four orientations, same recordings compared by two detection rules). Subject is a two-DOF robotic sensing antenna. The extracted table contains per-condition values (not per-event times); the difference column is a difference of published means and is not an individual latency measurement. Example trace delays in Table 9 are not added to the dataset. Exact timeseries files were not verified from the public paper.
primary_studies.rights: Publisher full text CC BY 4.0; source attribution in receipt. Only factual values and independently computed differences included.

primary_studies.title: Single sensor Wrist-Worn contact detection system for upper limb prosthetics using deep learning
primary_studies.reference: Metal probe closes a foil-covered, hand-held printed prosthesis circuit. Digital touch and wrist IMU are sampled together at 100 Hz. Each 20-sample classifier window uses a majority contact label. The window label and the first raw closure represent different endpoints. There is no six-axis wrist force–torque channel in the cited setup.
primary_studies.evidence: Published description with ten participants and 400 initial recordings. The article makes data available on reasonable request; no raw logs verified here. No request was sent, and no participant data retained.
primary_studies.rights: Article CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Only factual observations with attribution, no raw publication or participant data.
